Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Holiness 17:126: And nevertheless, the most agreed-upon repair for the conjugal time of Torah scholars is from Sabbath to Sabbath - and so it further says in the Tikkunim (page 21a): further, "every tree" (Genesis 1:11) - this is Tzaddik, who is "a fruit tree making fruit according to its kind," and this is the Sabbath day, for there is the union of the Shechinah with the Holy One, blessed be He, and there he has rest - and of it is said (Psalms 1:3), "and he shall be like a tree planted by streams of water, that yields its fruit in its season" - this is the "season" of Tzaddik, which is Sabbath eve, from which new souls blossom for Israel on Sabbath eve, called "new faces" - to this point.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Holiness 17:127: Further, in the Tikkunim (page 90a) it expounds there concerning forbidden relations, and it says afterward: and although all these forbidden relations are stated concerning the Sefirot and the Name YHVH, it is not in its supernal place - but rather, when the Shechinah is exiled, all the Sefirot descend with her, and there is no separation between her and the ten Sefirot, and when they descend they clothe themselves in the six weekdays, the six branches, and so on. And it said afterward, and why is there separation? Because Tzaddik, which is the sign of the covenant, is not there - and the secret of the matter, "there is no Tzaddik in the land" [play on Ecclesiastes 7:20], meaning the sign of the covenant is not there; but on the Sabbath, which is the seventh day, there is closeness and unification of the Name YHVH and all the Sefirot there - and therefore Torah scholars' conjugal time is from Sabbath eve to Sabbath eve, for forbidden relations certainly apply below, but above it is said (Psalms 5:5), "evil shall not sojourn with You." And Tzaddik, who unites with his wife on weekdays - that son he begets, of him it is said, "the righteous, yet it happens to him" [Ecclesiastes 8:14], for he causes the holy to become profaned, which is the seventh day, and at that time it is the secret of "the righteous, and it happens to him" - but above, there is no forbidden relation, cutting, or separation - to this point.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Holiness 17:128: And what it said, "that the holy becomes profaned," is explained: for the attribute of Tzaddik is called "the seventh day," and so it is explained in the Tikkunim (page 84a): but the dominion of Tzaddik is the seventh day, in which all the Sefirot are called "sevenths." And the reason is spelled out in the Tikkunim, Tikkun thirty, at the beginning of the Tikkun (page 73b) - see there, that its secret is the secret of the letter Zayin [seven], which is in Tzaddik, namely Yud over Vav, a crown upon his head - and since it is the seventh, it is holy, as explained in Tikkun 47 (page 84a), and one should not draw it into the profane, so as not to mix the holy with the profane - to this point.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Holiness 17:129: And so, from the repair of the sign of the covenant, secrets are revealed to whoever is righteous and fears Heaven, as it is written (Psalms 25:14), "the secret of the LORD is for those who fear Him." And so it says in the Tikkunim (Tikkunei Zohar Chadash, page 2a), found among us in manuscript: and whoever reveals secrets to the righteous causes Tzaddik to shine with the secrets of Torah and to the Shechinah, since [supernal] light is called "secret" [raz] - and at that time (Daniel 12:3), "and the wise shall shine like the brightness of the firmament" - to this point.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Holiness 17:130: And also the student shall repair his soul through the occupation with Torah by way of the secret [Kabbalah], as explained in the Tikkunim, Tikkun thirty (page 73b), concerning the punishment of those who withhold themselves from reading in the wisdom of Kabbalah - these are its words, in brief: those who make the Torah dry and do not wish to occupy themselves with wisdom, with Kabbalah, cause the spring, which is Yud, to depart from it, and only the letter Bet remains, dry - woe to them, who cause poverty, sword, plunder, killing, and destruction in the world - to this point; and we have copied its remaining words in the Introduction.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Holiness 17:131: And whoever reveals secrets of Torah to one unworthy - besides his punishment in the World to Come, he also has punishment in this world, that poverty pursues him - and so it says in the Zohar (beginning of Parashat Vayikra, page 2b), this letter stands for the punishment of one who reveals secrets, and your sign is "poverty and disgrace" - to this point.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Holiness 17:132: And so, in the Ra'aya Meheimna (Parashat Pinchas, page 244a), concerning what it wrote there, that one who throws crumbs on the ground is pursued by poverty - the Ra'aya Meheimna said, whoever treats bread crumbs with contempt and throws them where they are not needed - this applies all the more to whoever treats with contempt the "crumbs of the brain," which are of the seed, throwing them upon the ground, of which it is said (Genesis 6:12), "for all flesh had corrupted its way upon the earth" - or throws them into a menstruant, or "the daughter of a foreign god," or a maidservant, or a harlot; all the more so, all the more so, whoever treats with contempt the crumbs of Torah, which are the thorns of the letters and the crowns of the letters, of which it is said, whoever makes use of the crown shall pass away; all the more so whoever transmits the secrets of Torah, the secrets of Kabbalah, the secrets of the account of Creation, or the secrets of the letters of the Explicit Name, to people who are not fit, over whom the evil inclination rules, a harlot woman, of whom it is said (Proverbs 6:26), "for on account of a harlot woman one is reduced to a loaf of bread" - and there is no "bread" except Torah, and there is no "loaf" except a single halachah - to this point.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Holiness 17:133: And in the Ra'aya Meheimna (Parashat Eikev, page 272a) it explains that just as poverty pursues him concerning food, so poverty pursues him in attaining Torah - these are its words: and the vowel points of the holy Name are called "olive-sized crumbs," and these correspond to the drops of seed - and whoever treats them with contempt and throws them where they are not needed, poverty pursues him, and he goes wandering and fleeing - this is what is written (Job 15:23), "he wanders about for bread, where is it?" - and there is no "bread" except Torah, and he cries out, "where," meaning who shall have mercy on him, that he not be forgotten - and the olive-sized crumbs are in Tzaddik, who is pounded with the pounding of those olives - to this point.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Holiness 17:134: Also, among the attributes that merit the attribute of Tzaddik, one who rises early to be first at the synagogue stands at the level of Tzaddik - and so it is explained in the Zohar (Parashat Terumah, page 131a) - these are its words: and whoever comes early attaches himself to the Shechinah in one bond. Come and see, that first one found at the synagogue, who lingers at the synagogue, happy is his portion, for he stands at the level of Tzaddik together with the Shechinah - and this is (Proverbs 8:17), "and those who seek Me early [meshacharai] shall find Me" - this is an ascent of supernal ascent - to this point, relevant here.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Holiness 17:135: Further, one who merits the attribute of Tzaddik is one who gives charity, and this is explained in the Tikkunim as a repair for the sign of the covenant, and likewise to fulfill the mitzvah of Sabbath delight - these are the words of the Tikkunim (page 58a): further, the Shechinah is called Tzedakah [charity], and the Holy One, blessed be He, is the master of charity; in exile she is poor and her children are poor, and the Holy One, blessed be He, is, as it were, poor when He is away from His place - and concerning Him it is said (Isaiah 33:7), "behold, their valiant ones cry out outside" - and where is He poor and she poor? In Tzaddik, which is the covenant - and because Israel below sinned in it, this river dries up and becomes dry in the First and Second Temple, and the Shechinah is destroyed and dried up in it, because they caused the waters to be gathered away from it and the Shechinah remained dry - this is what is written (Genesis 1:9), "let the waters be gathered to one place, and let the dry land appear." And whoever gives charity to a poor person causes that river drawn from Eden, which is the supernal Mother, to water the garden, which is a "door" [dal], lifted up [dalah] for the poor. And the poor one is the Sabbath day, and whoever fulfills the mitzvah of Sabbath delight upon it causes that door to be watered, and that poor one is filled and called a river - and whoever has the means to fulfill Sabbath delight and does not do so turns the delight into the affliction of leprosy, and destroys his house and his wealth - to this point. And likewise concerning this punishment, it says at the end of page 18.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Holiness 17:136: Further, in Tikkun 24 (page 69b), concerning Sabbath delight: and one must fulfill in it the delight, which is Tzaddik, who comes forth from Eden, which is Binah, the World to Come, "to water" - this is the lower Shechinah, and the river is the Vav that comes forth from Yud-Hei and travels five hundred years, which are the five Sefirot, and reaches Tzaddik, to water from it the garden, which is Hei - and therefore "a man shall leave his father and his mother and cleave to his wife" (Genesis 2:24) - to this point.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Holiness 17:137: Further, concerning charity, that one merit the level of Tzaddik, it is explained in the Zohar (Parashat Behar Sinai, page 110b) - these are its words: "and if you say, what shall we eat" (Leviticus 25:20) - Rabbi Yehudah opened (Psalms 37:3), "trust in the LORD and do good; dwell in the land and cultivate faithfulness" - a person should always be careful of his Master and bind his heart with supernal faith, so that he be complete with his Master, for when he is complete with Him, none of the people of the world can harm him. Come and see, "trust in the LORD and do good" - rather, we have thus learned, through the deed below, the deed above is aroused - and this has already been established: "and you shall do them" - as it were, you shall make them, for it is your own arousal that you perform below, and it arouses above - and therefore "and do good" is written, and there is no "good" except Tzaddik, as it is written (Isaiah 3:10), "say of the righteous, that it is good" - since you perform [good deeds], this good is certainly aroused, and then, "dwell in the land and cultivate faithfulness" - and it is all one: "dwell in the land" - the supernal land [Malchut], for you cannot dwell with her until this "good" is aroused toward her; once it is aroused toward her, as it were He makes her His own, and then, "dwell in the land" - dwell within her, eat her fruit, delight with her. "And cultivate faithfulness" - this is the land, and it is all one, along the lines of (Psalms 92:3), "and Your faithfulness in the nights." "And cultivate faithfulness" - remember her in all your desires. And if you do not arouse toward her this "good," you distance yourself from her and do not draw near her - do not approach within, a burning fire; and if you approach her, do so with fear, like one who fears death, for then the fire burns and consumes the world with its flames; but once you arouse toward her this "good," then (Job 22:28), "you shall decree a matter, and it shall be established for you, and light shall shine upon your ways."
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Holiness 17:138: Come and see, people of faith conduct this desire every day - who are people of faith? Those who arouse this "good" toward it, and are not stingy with their own, and know that the Holy One, blessed be He, gives him more, along the lines of (Proverbs 11:24), "there is one who scatters, and yet increases." Why? Because this arouses blessings toward it, and he should not say, if I give this now, what shall I do tomorrow? Rather, the Holy One, blessed be He, gives him blessings without end, as they have established - to this point.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Holiness 17:139: And when the reader contemplates this teaching, he shall find that charity is a repair for the blemish of the sign of the covenant - the matter being that just as, through the sin of the blemish, the kindnesses depart from Tzaddik, who includes the five kindnesses, as explained in the Idra (page 142a), and it becomes a river that dries up and becomes dry, and therefore is called "good" - so through charity one draws the kindnesses to sweeten the judgments, and this is a complete unification, as explained in the teaching.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Holiness 17:140: And so it is explained further in the Zohar (Parashat Bechukotai, page 113b) - these are its words: Rabbi Shimon wept and said, woe to people who do not know and do not consider the honor of their Master - who makes the Name every day? Say, whoever gives charity to the poor. And at the end of his words: happy is the portion of whoever merits to make the holy Name above; therefore charity ascends above everything - and this applies to charity for its own sake, for it arouses Tzedakah toward Tzedek, to join us together as one, and that everything become the holy Name properly, since Tzedek is not repaired and completed except through charity, as it is written (Isaiah 54:14), "in righteousness you shall be established" - and this is said of Knesset Yisrael; therefore, "and you shall do them," and so on - to this point.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Holiness 17:141: And especially if he merits to be a collector of charity, he stands at the level of Tzaddik and receives reward equal to everyone - and so it is explained in the Zohar (Parashat Vayigash, page 208a), on the verse (Psalms 112:9), "he has scattered, he has given to the needy" - these are its words: and therefore, "he has scattered, he has given to the needy" - this is Tzaddik; "his righteousness endures forever" - this is Knesset Yisrael, for through this she stands in the secret of perfection, in complete existence; "the wicked shall see it and be grieved" - this is the kingdom of idol-worshippers. Come and see, the kingdom of Heaven is the Temple, to sustain all the poor within the shadow of the Shechinah, and Tzaddik is called "collector of charity," to show favor and to nourish everyone, as it is written, "he has scattered, he has given to the needy" - therefore collectors of charity receive reward equal to everyone - to this point. And the whole discourse on charity that we copied above is explained there, and we have not copied its words so as not to be lengthy.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Holiness 17:142: And also, he should intend, every day, to make himself righteous [Tzaddik], and give spiritual charity, as is written in the Tikkunim (page 33a) - these are its words: and these are those who give You a gift with the right hand, which is TZEDAKAH [charity]: Tzadi - ninety amens; Dalet - four sanctifications [kedushah responses]; Kof - one hundred blessings; Hei - five books of Torah - to this point. And elsewhere it explains that from TZADIK come ten holy [responses] that must be answered every day.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Holiness 17:143: Also, one who merits the attribute of Tzaddik is one who loves peace and pursues peace, as it is known that the attribute of Tzaddik is called "peace" (Zohar, Parashat Tzav, page 33a) - and just as he has separated peace [through his blemish], he should seek to mediate peace between a man and his wife, and between one person and his fellow. And so it is explained in the verses of King David, peace be upon him (Psalms 34:13-15), "who is the man who desires life, who loves days to see good?" - and it says, "turn from evil and do good; seek peace and pursue it." And the aspect of "loving days to see good" is a repair for the attribute of Tzaddik, and corresponding to it, it says, "turn from evil, seek peace and pursue it" - which is [directed at] one called an emitter of seed in vain, and "do good" - he shall establish the attribute of "good" through charity, as explained above, and likewise to juxtapose redemption to prayer, as explained (Berachot 10b), "and I have done what is good in Your eyes" (Isaiah 38:3), that he juxtaposed redemption to prayer. And the intent of "do good" is the repair of the attribute of "good," called Tzaddik, for the secret of unification, and therefore he must also seek peace, as explained, and this aspect is the "doing." And the aspect of "turn from evil," relating to the aspect of the blemish of Tzaddik, is guarding the tongue from everything that blemishes it, as explained above (in this chapter, and chapter 11) concerning "guard your tongue from evil" - for whoever blemishes his tongue is made impure by it, and there is no need to elaborate further on this.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Holiness 17:144: And included in the repair of the attribute of peace is that he hear his own disgrace and not respond - for since the attribute of peace is his accuser, he should accept the judgment of Heaven with a pleasant countenance. And David, because he sinned in the matter of Bathsheba, accepted his punishment when Shimi ben Gera disgraced him, and said (II Samuel 16:10), "the LORD has told him to curse," and he was silent.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Holiness 17:145: Also, for the repair of the sign of the covenant, one should lower his eyes, for through the sight of the eye the covenant is blemished, as it is written (Numbers 15:39), "and do not go about [tour] after your heart and after your eyes" - the heart and the eye are the two agents of transgression (Yerushalmi, Berachot, chapter 1, halachah 5). And when the eye is blemished it is called "an evil eye," as it says (Proverbs 23:6), "do not eat the bread of one with an evil eye" - and the reason is that just as the blemish of the covenant is called "evil," so the blemish in the house of the eye, which is the Yud, is called "evil," since it emits the sight of holiness in vain, toward a place of nakedness and the like. And since we find that the repair of the covenant is "turn from evil," it is included that one should not have an evil eye - and this is "turn from evil" without qualification, every aspect of evil, whether in the eye, or in the tongue, as it says, "guard your tongue from evil," or in the covenant - for in all of them "evil" applies precisely, as we have elaborated.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Holiness 17:146: And whoever guards his sight is bound to Chesed, for the lion [aryeh] is to the right, as explained in the Tikkunim several times (page 122a), and your sign is (Ezekiel 1:10), "and the face of a lion was on the right" - and "aryeh" [lion] relates to "re'iyah" [sight]. And Abraham our father, peace be upon him, because his intent was always to bind himself to the right, said (Genesis 12:11), "behold now, I know," and so on - and our Rabbis, of blessed memory, explained (Tanchuma, Lech Lecha 5) that he saw her reflection in the water. And all the aspects of the repairs of the eyes explained above are all repairs for the sign of the covenant, for Joseph holds fast to the eyes, as it is written (Genesis 49:22), "Joseph is a fruitful vine, a fruitful vine by a spring [alei ayin]" - and also in the aspect of the anatomy of the eye, Joseph's name is held fast, as explained in its place (Gate of Holiness, chapter 8). And especially since the seed is from the light of a person's eyes (Rambam, Hilchot De'ot, chapter 4, halachah 19), and since he blemishes the seed, a tear descends from his eyes, and the tear diminishes the seed, as explained in Tractate Gittin (70a), for the tear too is from the light of the eyes.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Holiness 17:147: Also, relevant to the repair of the attribute of Tzaddik is to be pious, and to be careful in all the attributes explained in the Gate of Love (chapter 11), which are the qualities that earn one the title "pious" - and the reason is that the attribute of Tzaddik is called Chesed, and so it is explained in the Idra (Parashat Naso, page 142a) - these are its words: and this cubit is called Chesed - and so at the end of the Idra of Ha'azinu (page 296a-b) - and since he blemished Chesed, it is fitting that he take hold of all the attributes of Chesed, as explained there.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Holiness 17:148: And happy is he who can fulfill the mortification that Rabbi Yishmael performed, as explained in Pirkei Heichalot, which we copied in the Gate of Repentance, chapter 5 - for by doing those things, he departs from the powers of judgment and severity and attaches himself to Chesed.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Holiness 17:149: And whoever merits the attribute of Tzaddik is the one who merits that the Shechinah rest upon him - for since the covenant is blemished, the blemish touches her, as explained, for the covenant includes circumcision and "peri'ah" [uncovering], which are Tzaddik and Tzaddik, as explained in Parashat Emor (page 91b). And after the repair of the covenant, it is a preparation to merit the land of the living, as it is said (Psalms 37:29), "the righteous shall inherit the land."
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Holiness 17:150: And so it further says in the Zohar (Parashat Shelach Lecha, page 160a), concerning the counsels of the inclination, it said, concerning the refutation of its counsels: what do the people of faith say? "If the LORD delights in us, He will give it to us" - once a person strives, with the desire of his heart, toward the Holy One, blessed be He, He requires from us only the heart, and let them guard that holy sign, as it is said (Isaiah 60:21), "and your people, all of them righteous, shall inherit the land forever" - to this point.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Holiness 17:151: Also, I have heard, concerning the repair of the sign of the covenant, that he should strive to bring people back to repentance, corresponding to the blemish of having emitted seed outward - for every drop of seed is a soul robbed by the hand of the external force - and therefore, corresponding to this, he should strive to take people who are held in the hand of the external force out of there and bring them within, to holiness, as King David, peace be upon him, said (Psalms 51:15), "I shall teach transgressors Your ways, and sinners shall return to You" - and it is known that Tzaddik is called "the language of teachings" [limudim], as explained in Parashat Pinchas (page 250a).
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Holiness 17:152: All these are particular aspects relating to the attribute of Tzaddik. But one must also repair all the aspects of the attributes for the whole "measure of stature," since the blemish of the covenant touches the whole measure of stature - for the covenant includes YHVH, which is the sum of the whole measure of stature, as explained above - and therefore Rashbi, peace be upon him, said (Zohar, Parashat Vayakhel, page 214b), which we copied above, concerning the blemish of the covenant: and these matters apply when he has not done a complete repentance, a repentance fitting to cover all his deeds. And at the end of his words: for there is no sin as difficult before the Holy One, blessed be He, as one who acts falsely and blemishes this holy sign of the covenant - of this sin it is written (Genesis 38:10), "and what he did was evil in the eyes of the LORD" - to this point.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Holiness 17:153: And the reason has already been explained above: that the Name YHVH is sealed in the covenant, as it says in the Tikkunim (page 65), "who shall go up for us to heaven" - the acrostic is MILAH, the final letters YHVH - and just as the Name YHVH is the root of all Names, as is known, so the covenant is the essential thing that sustains the whole body, and whoever blemishes it is as though he actually blemishes YHVH itself, which includes all the attributes. And therefore he needs a repentance fitting to cover all his deeds - meaning, as though he had blemished all his organs and all his deeds were blemished - and through this repentance he shall repair everything.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Holiness 17:154: And how is this so? He must perform mitzvot with all his organs. And so Rabbeinu Yonah, peace be upon him, wrote in Sha'arei Teshuvah (Gate 1) - these are its words: the tenth [principle]: to improve his deeds in the matter in which he acted wantonly - if he gazed at forbidden nakedness, he shall conduct himself with lowered eyes. If he sinned with an evil tongue, he shall occupy himself with Torah. And with all the organs with which he sinned he shall strive to fulfill mitzvot through them. And so our Rabbis, of blessed memory, said (Shemot Rabbah 23:3), the righteous are appeased through the very matter in which they sin. Further they said (Vayikra Rabbah 21:4), if you committed bundle after bundle of transgressions, perform corresponding to them bundle after bundle of mitzvot: feet swift to run to evil - let them run to a matter of mitzvah; a lying tongue - "his palate shall speak truth," and "his mouth shall open with wisdom, and the Torah of kindness is on his tongue"; hands that shed blood - "he shall surely open his hand to his poor"; haughty eyes - let them be lowly, and eyes cast down; a heart that devises wicked plans - in his heart he shall hide the words of Torah, and let the meditation of his heart be understanding; one who sends forth strife among brothers - he shall seek peace and pursue it - to this point.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Holiness 17:155: And so our Rabbis, of blessed memory, explained the verse (Ecclesiastes 7:19), "wisdom strengthens the wise more than ten rulers" - and other teachings concerning this matter we copied in this Gate, chapter 5; see there.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Holiness 17:156: And along these lines, he must be merciful and humble, corresponding to the first [sefirah, Chesed]; be wise, corresponding to the second [Gevurah/Binah]; and so purify his thoughts and be understanding and a penitent, corresponding to the third attribute [Da'at]; a bestower of kindness, corresponding to the fourth attribute [Chesed proper]; mighty, subduing his inclination, corresponding to the fifth attribute [Gevurah]; a master of Torah for its own sake, as explained concerning rising at midnight, corresponding to the sixth attribute [Tiferet]; one of those who support Torah scholars, corresponding to the seventh and eighth attributes [Netzach and Hod]; a guardian of the covenant properly, as explained, corresponding to the ninth attribute [Yesod]; he should intend in the covering of tzitzit, corresponding to the tenth attribute [Malchut] - and likewise the very existence of the mitzvah is for its repair, especially if he accepts suffering upon himself with the intent to purify himself from the husks he blemished with it - and likewise that he set fixed times for Torah, corresponding to her conjugal time, she being the King's daughter. And there are several further details relevant to the repair of the tenth attribute, some of which we have already explained in the Gate of Love.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Holiness 17:157: And whoever merits to purify the attribute of the covenant with all the conditions explained shall merit that his thoughts be pure and merit to cleave to YHVH. And the reason is that the supernal Yud, which is in the secret of Chochmah, depends on the lower Yud - this is the secret of the two Yuds within the Aleph, and likewise the two Yuds in the two Names YHVH and Adonai, as explained in the Tikkunim - and since the lower one is blemished, the supernal one too is blemished, and as long as a person does not repent to purify the blemished attribute of the covenant, it is impossible for his thoughts to be pure enough to cleave to YHVH while standing in prayer - and whoever purifies his covenant, as it were purifies the YHVH within him, and merits to cleave to Him.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Holiness 17:158: And so it is explained in the Zohar (Parashat Lech Lecha, page 94a), that concerning the attribute of the covenant it is said (Deuteronomy 4:4), "but you who cleave to YHVH your God" - and everything depends on this sign - and therefore it is written (Job 19:26), "and from my flesh I shall behold God" - this is the completeness of everything, "from my flesh" precisely, from this very sign precisely. And therefore, happy are Israel, who hold fast to Him, the Holy One, blessed be He - happy are they in this world and in the World to Come; of them it is written, "but you who cleave to YHVH," and so on, "you are all alive today."
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Holiness 17:159: And so in the Zohar (Parashat Vayikra, page 14b) - these are its words: but Israel, holy ones, children of holy ones, of stock and roots, were sweetened with complete, holy faith, at the time [Abraham] was circumcised, resting upon everyone - as it is written, "but you who cleave to YHVH your God, you are all alive today" - to this point. May the Name grant us the merit to be among those who guard His covenant and His commandments, that we cleave to Him.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Holiness 17:160: And with this the chapter concludes, and this Gate concludes:
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Humility 1:1: In explaining the word "humility" [anavah] and its merits: the word anavah is derived from the language of "poor" [ani] and "afflicted" [anui], the intent being submission - for the word "ani" means "submissive," and so (Exodus 10:3), "how long will you refuse to submit [le'anot] before Me?" is translated [in Targum] as "to submit yourself." And likewise "affliction" [inui] and "fasting" [ta'anit] are similar, as it says (I Kings 2:26), "and because you were afflicted in all that my father was afflicted" - and the like, many times; in all of them the intent is the matter of submission.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Humility 1:2: Now, the matter of submission and affliction is found in the Creator, blessed be He - for although He is exalted above all the exalted and prouder than all the proud, as Scripture says (Psalms 93:1), "the LORD reigns, He is clothed in pride" - humility is also attributed to Him, as King David, peace be upon him, said (ibid. 18:36), "and Your humility [anvatcha] has made me great" - and it is explained in Midrash Tanchuma (Yalkut Shim'oni on Samuel, remez 161) on this verse: they, of blessed memory, said, "and Your right hand has upheld me" (ibid.) - this is Torah, "from His right hand, a fire of law for them" (Deuteronomy 33:2). "And Your humility has made me great" - is there anyone more humble than the Holy One, blessed be He? A person says to his fellow, come adorn brides, visit the sick, bury the dead, comfort mourners - and he says to him, I am great and wealthy, and I am going; but the Holy One, blessed be He, "and He built the rib" (Genesis 2:22), "and the LORD appeared to him" (ibid. 18:1), "and He buried him in the valley" (Deuteronomy 34:6), "and God appeared to Jacob" (Genesis 35:9).
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Humility 1:3: Rabbi Abba bar Acha said, the student sits to learn before his teacher, and when he finishes, the student says to the teacher, I have wearied you. But Israel used to learn from the Holy One, blessed be He, and when they departed, the Holy One, blessed be He, said to them, I have greatly wearied you, as it is said (Deuteronomy 1:6), "the LORD our God spoke to us at Horeb, saying," and so on - hence, "and Your humility has made me great."
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Humility 1:4: Rabbi Shimon the Nazirite says, the student says to the teacher, come teach me one chapter, and the teacher says to him, I arrived before you at such-and-such place [i.e. he waits for the teacher]. But the Holy One, blessed be He, said to Ezekiel (Ezekiel 3:22), "arise, go out to the valley" - Ezekiel went out and found that the Holy One, blessed be He, had preceded him, as it is said (ibid. 3:23), "and I went out to the valley, and behold, the glory of the LORD stood there" - hence, "and Your humility has made me great."
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Humility 1:5: Lulyani bar Savrei in the name of Rabbi Yitzchak: see the humility that is in the Holy One, blessed be He - see what is written there (Exodus 19:19), "Moses would speak, and God would answer him with a voice" - it should have said only, "God would speak, and Moses would answer him with a voice" - hence, "and Your humility has made me great."
